text: A question arises in Genesis 22, and no answer is given. Abraham is commanded to take his son, his only son, the son whom he loves; and no account is given of what passes in him. The narrator does not enter his mind. Abraham makes no protest and attempts no bargain. Of the man who pleaded for Sodom nothing appears here. Abraham is presented less as a character than as a silence; and that silence is the central point of the chapter.
